edition.name: Migne, Patrologia Latina (PL 2, Paris 1844), De praescriptionibus adversus haereticos, via Latin Wikisource transcription
edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: Hinc igitur dirigimus praescriptionem: si Dominus Jesus Christus Apostolos misit ad praedicandum, alios non esse recipiendos praedicatores, quam Christus instituit; quia nec alius Patrem novit nisi Filius, et cui Filius revelavit, nec aliis videtur revelasse Filius, quam Apostolis quos misit ad praedicandum, utique quod illis revelavit. Quid autem praedicaverint, id est, quid illis Christus revelaverit, et hic praescribam non aliter probari debere, nisi per easdem ecclesias, quas ipsi Apostoli condiderunt, ipsi eis praedicando, tam viva, quod aiunt, voce, quam per epistolas postea. Si haec ita sunt, constat proinde omnem doctrinam quae cum illis ecclesiis apostolicis, matricibus et originalibus fidei, conspiret, veritati deputandam, sine dubio tenentem quod Ecclesiae ab Apostolis, Apostoli a Christo, Christus a Deo accepit; reliquam vero omnem doctrinam de mendacio praejudicandam, quae sapiat contra veritatem Ecclesiarum, et Apostolorum, et Christi, et Dei. Superest ergo uti demonstremus, an haec nostra doctrina, cujus regulam supra edidimus, de Apostolorum traditione censeatur, et hoc ipso, an caeterae de mendacio veniant. Communicamus cum ecclesiis apostolicis, quod nulli doctrina diversa: hoc est testimonium veritatis.
pass_a_gloss: From here, therefore, we direct our prescription: if Lord Jesus Christ sent Apostles to preach, other preachers are not to be received, except those whom Christ established; because neither does another know the Father except the Son, and to whom the Son revealed, nor does the Son seem to have revealed to others, except to the Apostles whom He sent to preach, certainly what He revealed to them. But what they preached, that is, what Christ revealed to them, I also prescribe that it ought to be proved not otherwise, except through the same churches, which the Apostles themselves founded, themselves preaching to them, both with living voice, as they say, and through letters afterwards. If these things are so, it is established, accordingly, that every doctrine which agrees with those apostolic churches, the matrices and originals of the faith, is to be reckoned to the truth, undoubtedly holding what the Churches received from the Apostles, the Apostles from Christ, Christ from God; but the rest of every doctrine is to be prejudged as a lie, which savors against the truth of the Churches, and the Apostles, and Christ, and God. It remains, therefore, for us to demonstrate, whether our doctrine, whose rule we published above, is considered from the tradition of the Apostles, and by this very fact, whether the others come from a lie. We communicate with the apostolic churches, because no other doctrine is diverse: this is the testimony of the truth.

choices.why: technical term for a legal or formal directive

choices.english: the matrices and originals of the faith
choices.why: metaphorical expression for the apostolic churches as the source of the faith

pass_b_english: So we lay down our rule: if the Lord Jesus Christ sent the Apostles to preach, then no other preachers are to be accepted except the ones Christ himself appointed. For no one knows the Father except the Son, and those to whom the Son chooses to reveal him. And the Son does not appear to have revealed the Father to anyone except the Apostles he sent to preach — precisely what he revealed to them. Now, what they preached — that is, what Christ revealed to them — I insist must be proved in no other way than through the very churches the Apostles themselves founded, preaching to them in person, as they say, with living voice, and later by their letters. If that is how it stands, then it follows that any doctrine which agrees with those apostolic churches — the matrices and originals of the faith — is to be counted as true, beyond doubt holding what the Churches received from the Apostles, the Apostles from Christ, Christ from God. But every other doctrine is to be prejudged as a lie, if it clashes with the truth of the Churches, the Apostles, Christ, and God. It remains, then, for us to demonstrate whether our own doctrine, whose rule we published above, is reckoned to come from the tradition of the Apostles — and by that very fact, whether the rest come from a lie. We are in communion with the apostolic churches, because our doctrine differs in no respect: this is the testimony of the truth.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text. Pass A and Pass B are consistent with the source. Pass B's slight stylistic variations (e.g., 'I insist' for 'hic praescribam' and 'clashes with' for 'sapiat contra') do not alter the theological or logical meaning of the original.
